03 Concept generation

BMED Chapter 5: divergence (generating ideas), then post-processing and confluence of ideas (5.5), concept iteration (5.6) and documenting concepts (5.11).

1. Divergence: the five concept briefs

The source document hemodynamic_app_concepts.docx proposes five ways to deploy the same model:

BriefClinical roleMain outputsBrief's own concern
1 Real-time deterioration alertWatches monitor signals; alerts on forecast deteriorationStable / Watch / Deteriorating / Critical; forecast MAP and ABP; R, C; signal qualityMust gate alerts by signal quality to avoid alarm fatigue and false confidence
2 Forecast dashboardShows current state and predicted trendMAP trend, ABP forecast curve, R, C, historyMay be less impactful if it only displays and never notifies
3 Intervention response monitorShows whether the patient improves after treatmentImproving / no clear response / possible worsening; ΔMAP, ΔR, ΔC; timelineNeeds reliable event timestamps; must support review, never prescribe
4 Non-invasive early warningECG + PPG when there is no arterial lineRisk score, estimated MAP, confidence, missing-input warningsLower certainty without ABP; must show confidence clearly
5 Decision-support review systemStores forecasts, alerts and markers for review, handoff, auditEpisode summaries, alert history, R/C trends, exportable reportLess useful at the bedside unless paired with real-time alerting

2. Functional decomposition

To see where the briefs overlap, each was broken into the functions it performs (a function–means view, BMED 5.7):

Function12345
F1 Acquire waveforms (ECG, PPG)●●●●○ stored
F2 Acquire invasive ABP●●●–○ stored
F3 Check signal quality●●●●●
F4 Forecast MAP / ABP 15 s ahead●●●●●
F5 Estimate R, C●●●●●
F6 Classify risk and raise an alert●––●–
F7 Explain the forecast visually○●○○●
F8 Detect and assess treatment response––●–●
F9 Record and export the episode––––●
Time of usereal timereal timereal timereal timeafter the event
SettingICU / ORICU / ORICU / ORstep-down / wardany

3. Confluence: why 1 + 2 + 3 merge and 4 and 5 stay separate

BMED 5.5 recommends grouping ideas that share a purpose and recombining partial solutions. The test applied here was simple: would the same user, at the same moment, with the same data, want these functions together?

  • Briefs 1, 2 and 3 → Concept A. All three serve the same bedside clinician, in real time, with an arterial line. Each covers a weakness the brief itself names in another:
    • 1 alerts but needs to show why → 2 supplies the forecast display (F7);
    • 2 displays but "may be less impactful if it does not notify" → 1 supplies the alert (F6);
    • 3 shows treatment response, which is what a clinician needs straight after acting on an alert from 1 (F8).

The brief recommended combining 1 and 3. This design goes one step further and also absorbs 2, because a dashboard on its own fails the brief's own impact concern. Inside an alerting app, the dashboard becomes the explanation for each alert (Nielsen heuristic 1, visibility of system status).

  • Brief 4 → Concept B. It has a different setting and a different input set (no ABP). Merging it into A would hide a large accuracy difference behind one interface. It stays a separate concept so that it can be evaluated on its own merits. (Concept A automatically falls back to the ECG + PPG regime if the arterial line fails, so B's engine also exists inside A as a degraded mode.)
  • Brief 5 → Concept C. It runs at a different time: after the event, not at the bedside. Its users (quality officers, the next shift) and its risks are different. It stays separate.

4. The three concepts

Concept A: Integrated monitorConcept B: Non-invasiveConcept C: Episode review
Combines briefs1 + 2 + 345
InputsABP + ECG + PPG + intervention eventsECG + PPGStored ABP, ECG, PPG, events
SettingICU, operating roomStep-down, recovery, lower resourceAny setting with records
ModeReal time, 1 s updatesReal time, 1 s updatesRetrospective batch
Key outputsAlert level with reason; 15 s forecast with uncertainty band; P(MAP < 65); R, C trends; intervention response; event logRisk score with confidence; estimated MAP; missing-input panel; alert capped at WATCHHandoff narrative; time in each state; alert episodes; intervention table; printable report, CSV, JSON
Shared engineVersion 5 model, risk controls RC-07 to RC-10, domain calibrationsamesame (runs Concept A's pipeline over the whole record)

All three share one engine (app/engine/). Differences between them therefore come from the concept, not from implementation quality. This matters for a fair selection (BMED 6.4: compare concepts on equal footing).

5. Concept iteration (BMED 5.6) during prototyping

Building working prototypes early (BMED 6.5.1, feasibility tests) changed the concepts before the final selection:

IterationFound byChange
B raised many false alarms when it used A's thresholdsfirst prototype runConfidence-capped priority: a low-confidence estimate can raise at most WATCH
The intervention channel cannot tell a vasopressor from a fluid bolusVersion 5 data inspectionResponse tracking driven by an event log, with confounding flags
VitalDB pump-rate data are sparse (missing values read as 0)real-data replaySample-and-hold of pump rate, used for event detection only
A 40% PPG drop-out passed the Version 5 quality gateverificationRC-07 raw-signal pre-check
Version 5 rejected genuine arterial pressure in profound shockverification (hazard H-09)RC-08 hold, RC-09 shock-aware check, RC-10 measured-pressure floor
Simulation calibration did not transfer to real patientsverificationDomain-specific calibration

6. Documentation

Each concept is documented as a running prototype (#/concept-a, #/concept-b, #/concept-c in the app). Screenshots are in docs/figures/ui0*.png, and the source is in app/.
